<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Medical image encryption is essential for protecting patient confidentiality and data integrity in telemedicine, cloud-based healthcare systems, and remote diagnostic workflows. Although many recent image encryption schemes rely on chaos-based permutation and diffusion mechanisms, their security often depends on heuristic randomness properties, plaintext-dependent parameter generation, or loosely coupled integrity verification. This paper presents a standards-based medical image encryption framework that integrates established cryptographic primitives into a plaintext-independent, authenticated design tailored to medical image protection. The proposed framework derives independent encryption, permutation, and authentication keys using HKDF from a shared master secret and a fresh session nonce. ChaCha20 is then used for keystream generation, while a chained diffusion mechanism enhances plaintext sensitivity and supports strong avalanche behavior. To provide integrity and authenticity, HMAC-SHA256 binds the ciphertext, nonce, and plaintext digest using an encrypt-then-MAC structure. The scheme was evaluated on CT, MRI, and X-ray images using standard statistical, differential, correlation, key-sensitivity, tamper-detection, and execution-time analyses. Experimental results show near-ideal entropy, low adjacent-pixel correlation, NPCR and UACI values close to theoretical expectations, reliable tamper detection, and practical execution time across the tested modalities. The results indicate that standardized cryptographic primitives, when combined with image-specific permutation and chained diffusion, can provide an effective and practical framework for secure medical image transmission.</jats:p>
title: A standards-based framework for medical image encryption using ChaCha20, HKDF, and integrated HMAC authentication
